newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's PHIBOR mixed, short-term rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Manila's PHIBOR mixed, short-term rates fall.

text.p: Philippine interbank offered rates (PHIBOR) continued to be mixed on Wednesday, with the one week to one month rates lower, while the rest were steady or higher.
Traders said PHIBOR were reflective of the current trends in the market. Short-term rates fell following the stability in the overnight market, they said.
"Banks are now willing to lend out their pesos for the short term," a foreign bank dealer said.
But the six-month and one-year rates increased, mirroring the rise in Treasury bill rates in last Monday's weekly auction, traders said.
The two-month and three-month rates were unchanged following a readjustment on Tuesday in line with the T-bill trend.
PHIBOR represents the rates at which banks would like to swap their pesos for dollars.
